variations.name: Panelized / prefabricated deep energy retrofit (Energiesprong model)
variations.description: Factory-built insulated facade and roof panels — often with integrated windows, ventilation or HVAC pods — are scanned-to-fit and clipped onto existing buildings in days, cutting the cost and disruption of net-zero renovation enough to make whole-portfolio social-housing retrofits repeatable.

companies.name: Energiesprong Foundation
companies.what: Dutch-born market-development organization that standardizes performance-guaranteed panelized net-zero retrofits and aggregates social-housing demand across NL/DE/FR/UK/US.
companies.signal: 10,000+ buildings retrofitted across Europe and North America with 70-80% energy reduction

companies.name: ecoworks
companies.what: Berlin general contractor that digitally plans and robot-prefabricates facade elements plus rooftop PV to take apartment blocks to net zero in roughly 7-10 days of on-site work.
companies.signal: €40M Series A (2024) plus €23M (Mar 2026) to deliver Germany's largest cooperative serial renovation

companies.name: Renowate
companies.what: Joint venture of listed German landlord LEG Immobilien and builder Rhomberg industrializing serial refurbishment for housing portfolios in NRW and beyond.
companies.signal: JV backed by a major listed landlord; growing serial-renovation pipeline in Germany

companies.name: Factory Zero
companies.what: Dutch manufacturer of integrated energy modules (heat pump, ventilation, PV electronics in one rooftop pod) and prefab roofs used in Energiesprong renovations.
companies.signal: Core component supplier in the Netherlands, the model's most industrialized market

companies.name: Q-Bot
companies.what: UK robots crawl under suspended floors and spray-apply insulation, retrofitting hard-to-treat homes without ripping up floors.
companies.signal: Thousands of UK homes insulated via partners including utilities and councils; BBA-certified process

companies.name: Hydronic Shell Technologies
companies.what: Facade-integrated mechanical systems: overclad panels carry hydronic HVAC distribution so multifamily towers electrify without entering apartments.
companies.signal: NYSERDA-backed demonstrations including a Bronx overclad project and a Syracuse pilot

companies.name: Dextall
companies.what: NYC startup making software-designed prefabricated unitized wall panels for recladding and deep-retrofit projects as well as new builds.
companies.signal: Venture-backed; panels cut facade installation time dramatically on NYC multifamily projects

companies.name: Melius Homes
companies.what: UK design-build contractor that delivered Britain's first Energiesprong-style whole-house retrofits for social landlords (Nottingham's Destination Zero).
companies.signal: Pioneer Energiesprong UK delivery partner since 2017

variations.white_space: Outside Dutch/German social housing the field is nearly empty — the US has no at-scale panelized-retrofit vendor (NYSERDA's RetrofitNY struggled to get bids that pencil) because fragmented ownership, custom facades and cheap gas stretch paybacks; building-performance-standard fines (LL97/BERDO) plus scan-to-fab mass customization create the opening for a US serial-retrofit integrator.

variations.name: Whole-home electrification platforms & tech-enabled installers
variations.description: One-stop platforms plan, finance and install heat pumps, heat-pump water heaters, panel upgrades and EV chargers — using remote assessment, instant quoting and incentive capture to compress a fragmented multi-contractor journey into a single offer, which is why they dominate heat-pump growth in Europe.

companies.name: Aira
companies.what: Swedish direct-to-consumer heat-pump installer (founded by Northvolt's Vargas) selling monthly clean-energy plans across UK, Germany and Italy with its own Wroclaw factory.
companies.signal: €150M equity (Aug 2025) on top of ~€145M Series B and €200M BNP Paribas debt (2024)

companies.name: Enpal
companies.what: German solar-and-heat-pump installer that rents systems with zero upfront cost and refinances customer contracts via securitization.
companies.signal: €1.1B ABS facility (Mar 2025, Barclays/BofA/CACIB); ~5,000 heat pumps in 18 months making it Germany's #1 installer; >€5B debt raised; profitable

companies.name: 1KOMMA5°
companies.what: Roll-up of dozens of local installers across DACH/Nordics/Australia selling solar + heat pump + storage unified by its Heartbeat energy-management OS.
companies.signal: €150M pre-IPO round (Dec 2025); ~€400M equity raised; IPO targeted 2026

companies.name: Elephant Energy
companies.what: Denver/Boston climate-comfort general contractor: builds homeowners an Electrification Roadmap then manages heat-pump installs through vetted subcontractors.
companies.signal: $3.5M seed led by Building Ventures (Mar 2025) plus $2.38M follow-on (2026)

companies.name: QuitCarbon

companies.name: Zero Homes

companies.name: Quilt

companies.name: Octopus Energy

companies.name: BOXT

companies.name: Conduit Tech

companies.name: ServiceTitan

companies.name: Wrightsoft

companies.name: CoolCalc

variations.white_space: The category leader was absorbed by ServiceTitan within two years of seed, signaling consolidation into field-service suites; a standalone wedge remains in automated heat-pump design-to-permit (room-by-room sizing, duct mods, electrical load calc, and rebate paperwork in one pass), which furnace-swap-oriented incumbents still don't serve.

variations.name: Heat-as-a-service & subscription comfort models

companies.name: Thermondo

companies.name: Hometree

companies.name: E.ON

companies.name: Palmetto (LightReach)

companies.name: Sealed

variations.white_space: True 'heat by the month' barely exists outside boiler-rental cultures (Germany/UK): homeowner credit risk, weather-dependent savings and long service tails killed US pioneer Sealed's pay-for-savings model, and US TPO leases are only now reaching HVAC via Palmetto — an opening for utility tariffed-on-bill heat or insurer-grade comfort subscriptions in North America.
